title: Putting a collection into albums without losing track
target: How albums and binder pages work in TCG Card Shop Simulator: a card knows when it belongs to an album, a binder page has its own index and visibility, and the binder has a flip animation of its own.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: An album or binder to put them in
A plan for what the album is for

steps.do: Decide what the album is for before you start filling it, because the game keeps albums as things of their own.
steps.because: an album is a thing of its own in the game (CardAlbum)

steps.do: Put a card in the album rather than on a shelf when it is for keeping, because a card carries a flag for being an album card.
steps.because: a card carries a flag for whether it is an album card (m_IsCardAlbumCard)

steps.do: Work page by page, because a binder page has an index of its own.
steps.because: a binder page has an index that can be set (CardAlbumPage, BinderPage)

steps.do: Show and hide pages deliberately, because a page has a visibility the game can set.
steps.because: a binder page has its visibility set on its own (BinderPage)

steps.do: Count what is in the album as you go, because the album keeps a count of the cards in it.
steps.because: the album carries a card count (AlbumCardCount)

steps.do: Expect the binder to turn like an object, because it has a flip animation of its own.
steps.because: it can carry the collection binder's flip animation (m_CollectionBinderFlipAnimCtrl)

steps.do: Know that the page art is the game's own, because the binder page is a texture the build ships.
steps.because: the build ships its own binder page texture (T_BinderPage)

steps.do: Leave room for the pocket pages the game ships, because there is more than one page kind.
steps.because: a nine-pocket page texture is shipped as well (T_3_UP_PlatinumSeriesPocketPages)

commonMistakes: Filling an album with stock that was meant to be sold.
Moving a page's contents card by card instead of working page by page.
Forgetting that a card has to be flagged as an album card before it belongs there.
Treating the album as a shelf and expecting the shop's stock counts to agree.
Leaving pages hidden and then wondering where a card went.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Identifiers are listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
